question: What must I do if I think a cosmetic product I already placed on the market does not comply with the regulation?
answer: If you are the responsible person and consider or have reason to believe the product is not in conformity, you must immediately take the necessary corrective measures to bring it into conformity, withdraw it, or recall it [Reg 1223/2009 | Article 5, p. 8]. If the product presents a risk to human health, you must also immediately inform the competent national authorities of the Member States where you made the product available and where the product information file is accessible, detailing the non-compliance and measures taken [Reg 1223/2009 | Article 5, p. 8]. Additionally, you must cooperate with those authorities on any action to eliminate the risks [Reg 1223/2009 | Article 5, p. 8].

question: Once my cosmetic is on sale in the EU, what do I have to send to the notification portal about how the product looks?
answer: You must submit the original labelling corresponding to the first placing on the market, as well as a photograph of the original packaging where reasonably legible [CPNP guide | p. 32]. The labelling must include all mandatory elements of Article 19, plus any enclosed or attached leaflets, labels, tags, or cards if applicable [CPNP guide | p. 33]. These must be attached in PDF, JPG, or JPEG format, with a total size not exceeding 2 MB [CPNP guide | p. 32, 33].

question: I'm hiring someone to sign off the safety assessment of my cosmetic, what qualifications does this person need?
answer: The safety assessor must hold a diploma or other evidence of formal qualifications awarded upon completing a university course of theoretical and practical study in pharmacy, toxicology, medicine, or a similar discipline, or a course recognised as equivalent by a Member State [Reg 1223/2009 | Article 10, p. 9]. They must also be a professional possessing the necessary knowledge and expertise to draw up an accurate safety assessment [Decision 2013/674 | Section 4.4, p. 21].

question: Before I start selling my cosmetic, what do I need to have done about its safety?
answer: Prior to placing a cosmetic product on the market, the responsible person must ensure that the product has undergone a safety assessment and that a cosmetic product safety report is set up in accordance with Annex I [Reg 1223/2009 | Article 10, p. 9]. This assessment must take into account the intended use of the product, the anticipated systemic exposure to individual ingredients, and use an appropriate weight-of-evidence approach [Reg 1223/2009 | Article 10, p. 9]. Furthermore, the safety assessment (Part B of the report) must be carried out by a qualified safety assessor [Decision 2013/674 | Section 3.10, p. 18].

question: Do I need to update my cosmetic's safety report once it is already on sale?
answer: Yes, you must ensure that the cosmetic product safety report is kept up to date in view of additional relevant information generated subsequent to placing the product on the market [Reg 1223/2009 | Article 10, p. 9]. The safety assessment must be reviewed and, if necessary, updated when legal requirements change, new scientific or toxicological data become available, raw material formulations or specifications change, conditions of use change, or there is a rising trend in undesirable effects [Decision 2013/674 | Section 4.3.2 (part 3), p. 21].

question: Can I sell my cosmetic in the EU if the final formula or its ingredients were tested on animals?
answer: Placing on the market of cosmetic products is prohibited if their final formulation or their ingredients have been the subject of animal testing using methods other than validated alternative methods in order to meet the requirements of Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 [Reg 1223/2009 | Article 18, p. 13-14]. Furthermore, performing animal testing of finished cosmetic products or ingredients within the Community to meet the requirements of this Regulation is also prohibited [Reg 1223/2009 | Article 18, p. 13-14].

question: My face cream lasts more than 30 months before it goes off, do I still need to print an expiry date on the label?
answer: The indication of the date of minimum durability is not mandatory for cosmetic products with a minimum durability of more than 30 months [Reg 1223/2009 | Article 19 (part 2), p. 15]. For such products, you must instead indicate the period of time after opening for which the product is safe and can be used without any harm to the consumer, unless the concept of durability after opening is not relevant [Reg 1223/2009 | Article 19 (part 3), p. 15].

question: For how long do I have to keep the paperwork about my cosmetic after I stop selling it?

question: Can I write on my moisturiser's label that it erases wrinkles even if it doesn't really do that?

Presentations of a product's performance must not go beyond the available supporting evidence [Reg 655/2013 | Section 4: Honesty, p. 3].

question: A customer tells me my face cream gave her a serious allergic reaction, what do I have to do?
answer: In the event of serious undesirable effects, the responsible person and distributors must without delay notify the competent authority of the Member State where the effect occurred of all known or reasonably expected serious undesirable effects, the product name for specific identification, and any corrective measures taken [Reg 1223/2009 | Article 23, p. 16-17]. question: My product has a different name in each country where I sell it, how do I show that when I notify it?
answer: When the product is made available with a name translated in different languages, each of these names has to be mentioned in the notification together with its corresponding language selected via the selection box [CPNP guide | p. 17 (part 1)]. If the name is the same for some languages but different in others, all linguistic versions of the product name must be entered individually in the system, indicating the corresponding language for each [CPNP guide | p. 17 (part 1)].

question: My cosmetic contains an ingredient classified as possibly causing cancer, where do I declare that when I notify it?

question: I sell a kit where the customer has to mix two parts before using it, what extra questions will the notification portal ask me?

question: I want to write on my cream's box that it "firms skin in 7 days", what rules do I have to follow?

question: I import my cosmetics from outside the EU, who counts as the responsible person and what do they have to upload to the notification portal about the label?
